title: Short vs Long Vowels
subtitle: Ship/Sheep, Full/Fool, Bit/Beat
description: English vowel length can completely change a word's meaning. Training your mouth and ear on these minimal pairs is essential for clear, natural pronunciation.
tip: For long vowels, hold the sound a beat longer and feel your mouth move slightly — for short vowels, keep it crisp, brief, and relaxed.
phrases: The sheep can't sleep on the slip of the ship.
Pull the pool cover over — don't fool around in the full tub.
Did you feel the fill line? Sit in your seat, not on the bit of wood.
The wheel needs a will to spin — beat the drum, don't just bit it.
He'll slip into sleep the second he sits in his seat.
The fool fell into the full bucket near the pool.
She can feel it fill up as she sits and beats the rhythm.
The sheep on the ship slipped while the crew tried to sleep.
